item.title: Government pays tribute to late Agni Deo Singh with i-Reguregu
item.description: Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Industries, Commerce and Business Development, Manoa Kamikamica , led the Government delegation in extending condolences to the late Minister’s family. The Deputy Prime Minister reflected on Singh’s dedicated service to Fiji, saying he would be deeply missed by the Prime Minister, his Cabinet colleagues and those who had worked alongside him.
item.content:encoded:
Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Industries, Commerce and Business Development, Manoa Kamikamica , led the Government delegation in extending condolences to the late Minister’s family.

The Deputy Prime Minister reflected on Singh’s dedicated service to Fiji, saying he would be deeply missed by the Prime Minister, his Cabinet colleagues and those who had worked alongside him.

Kamikamica thanked the family for supporting a father who served his country with honour and distinction.

The i-reguregu was also attended by the Minister for iTaukei Affairs, Ifereimi Vasu; Minister for Immigration, Viliame Naupoto; Minister for Finance, Esrom Immanuel; Acting Attorney-General and Minister for Justice, Siromi Turaga; Minister for Women, Children and Social Protection, Sashi Kiran; Assistant Minister in the Office of the Prime Minister, Sakiusa Tubuna; Permanent Secretaries; and Government officials from various ministries.

The Fiji Government extended its heartfelt condolences to Singh’s family and acknowledged his years of dedicated service to Fiji.

item.title: From Batiki to maritime leadership as Lesianawai takes on senior MSAF role
item.description: Lesianawai has been appointed Manager Governance, Legal and Board Secretary at MSAF. The IMO-International Maritime Law Institute congratulated Lesianawai on her appointment after she graduated from the Institute earlier this year with a Master of Laws in International Maritime Law.
item.content:encoded:
Lesianawai has been appointed Manager Governance, Legal and Board Secretary at MSAF.

The IMO-International Maritime Law Institute congratulated Lesianawai on her appointment after she graduated from the Institute earlier this year with a Master of Laws in International Maritime Law.

Her appointment follows a successful academic year, during which she was selected to deliver the valedictory address on behalf of the Institute’s 2025–2026 graduating class.

She also received the Best Performance Prize in recognition of her academic performance.

Lesianawai has family ties to Vuna in Taveuni through her father and Yavu Village in Batiki through her mother.

She spent part of her childhood in Batiki and attended Batiki District School, growing up in a maritime community where the sea plays an important role in everyday life and provides a vital connection to other parts of Fiji.

Her journey has since taken her from Batiki to postgraduate studies in international maritime law, and now to a senior role with the Maritime Safety Authority of Fiji.
